checklist.name: corneal opacity
quotes: Corneal opacity is often the first clinically recognized sign of LCAT deficiency and was present in all FLD and FED patients at the time of report
Diffuse corneal opacity, in association with extremely low HDL-C levels, is pathognomonic for both forms of LCAT deficiency
checklist.why: Defining sign of both forms (FLD and FED) and usually the first one noticed.

checklist.name: low hdl cholesterol
quotes: HDL-C levels were uniformly low in both FLD and FED patients
Both are characterized by very low levels of HDL-C and corneal opacities
checklist.why: Defining laboratory finding of both forms; case reports almost always give the value.

checklist.name: low apolipoprotein a-i or a-ii
quotes: the primary HDL proteins, were markedly decreased in both FLD and FED patients
levels of ApoA-II, another HDL protein, were also markedly reduced
checklist.why: HDL apolipoproteins are markedly reduced in both forms and often reported beside HDL-C.

checklist.name: hypertriglyceridemia
quotes: Triglyceride (TG) levels were elevated in both groups.
TG levels were elevated in both FLD and FED patients.
checklist.why: Common lipid abnormality in both forms, routinely reported in lipid panels.

checklist.name: elevated unesterified (free) cholesterol
quotes: Plasma UC was approximately 2-fold higher than the reference threshold in FLD patients
approximately 1.2-fold higher in FED patients
checklist.why: Marker of impaired esterification; markedly raised in FLD, mildly in FED, and linked to severe renal disease in FLD.

checklist.name: reduced cholesteryl ester fraction
quotes: Plasma EC% (percent of EC:TC) was approximately 5.4-fold below the lowest limit of the reference range in FLD
EC% represents the most promising diagnostic biomarker in the clinical setting
checklist.why: Low esterified-cholesterol percentage is the clinical-laboratory marker that best separates FLD (very low) from FED (near normal).

checklist.name: low ldl cholesterol or apolipoprotein b
quotes: LDL-C and apoB levels were significantly lower in FLD compared with FED.
checklist.why: Mainly FLD; the review names it as a difference between the two forms.

checklist.name: lipoprotein x
quotes: The presence of LpX was reported in 32 of the 36 FLD patients where measured.
An abnormal lipoprotein (lipoprotein X [LpX]) has been frequently observed in FLD
checklist.why: Abnormal lipoprotein found in most FLD patients tested and proposed as the cause of renal damage; rarely tested in FED.

checklist.name: anemia
quotes: FLD patients had a significantly higher prevalence of anemia compared with FED patients
causing increased fragility and hemolytic anemia
checklist.why: Present in most FLD and a minority of FED patients; a hemolytic anemia from red-cell membrane changes.

checklist.name: proteinuria
quotes: Proteinuria and hematuria were the first signs of renal impairment
Proteinuria, n/N (%)^b | 119/136 (87.5)
checklist.why: First and most frequent sign of renal disease in FLD; absent in FED by the review's classification.

checklist.name: hematuria
quotes: Hematuria, n/N (%)^b | 44/46 (95.7)
Our data confirm that the first sign of renal disease in FLD is proteinuria or hematuria
checklist.why: Early sign of renal disease in FLD, frequent where reported.

checklist.name: nephrotic syndrome
quotes: Clinical presentation of the renal disease is that of nephrotic syndrome
checklist.why: The review gives nephrotic syndrome as the clinical presentation of FLD renal disease; case reports often name it rather than proteinuria alone.

checklist.name: chronic kidney disease or renal failure
quotes: FLD is more severe and characterized by early and progressive chronic kidney disease (CKD)
Notably, FLD patients, but not FED patients, develop early and progressive CKD leading to ESRD
followed by rapid decline of renal function
checklist.why: Mainly FLD: the main cause of morbidity and the feature that separates FLD from FED.

checklist.name: atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease
quotes: Risk of developing atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) is variable and still debated
our study suggests that FLD patients have reduced prevalence of ASCVD, compared with FED patients
checklist.why: Reported in both forms, more often in FED; case reports often state presence or absence of coronary or other atherosclerotic disease.

checklist.name: glomerular sclerosis
quotes: histological characteristics include segmental glomerular sclerosis
Global and/or segmental glomerular sclerosis | 18/20 (90.0)
checklist.why: Core FLD kidney biopsy finding (segmental or global).

checklist.name: mesangial expansion or mesangial lipid deposits
quotes: notable findings included expansion and vacuolization of the mesangial area with electron microscopy revealing high-density lipid deposits
Mesangial deposits | 26/26 (100.0)
checklist.why: FLD biopsy finding present in nearly every biopsy that described the mesangium.

checklist.name: glomerular basement membrane thickening or lipid deposits
quotes: depositions of foamy material in the glomerular basement membrane leading to irregular thickening
Thickening of the GBM | 24/24 (100.0)
checklist.why: FLD biopsy finding the review calls characteristic of LCAT deficiency.

checklist.name: glomerular foam cells
quotes: Foam cell infiltration | 20/25 (80.0)
Mesangial foam cell infiltration | 6/8 (75.0)
checklist.why: Frequent FLD biopsy finding, a cellular change distinct from the extracellular deposits above.

checklist.name: podocyte foot process effacement
quotes: Podocyte foot processes were described as fused or effaced.
Effacement of podocyte foot processes | 9/9 (100.0)
checklist.why: FLD electron-microscopy finding present in every biopsy that reported it.

checklist.name: tubular atrophy or interstitial fibrosis
quotes: Tubular atrophy | 13/15 (86.7)
Interstitial fibrosis | 10/13 (76.9)
checklist.why: Tubulointerstitial damage on FLD biopsy, reflecting more advanced disease.

left_out: reduced plasma LCAT concentration or LCAT activity: the causal enzyme defect itself, present by definition
end-stage renal disease and kidney transplantation (and recurrence in the graft): outcomes; ESRD is covered by 'chronic kidney disease or renal failure'
glomerular C3 or IgM deposits on immunofluorescence: the review calls immunofluorescence results mixed and reported in few biopsies
pseudothrombi, hyalinosis, intimal thickening and subendothelial deposits (vessels): rarely reported; the review calls pseudothrombi sporadic

vacuolization of glomerular cells, GBM or tubules, duplication of the GBM, interstitial inflammation, interstitial macrophages, interstitial edema: further biopsy detail, kept to six biopsy items to avoid overlap
cardiovascular disease of other nature: not specified by the review
elevated total or non-HDL cholesterol: the review links higher levels to severe CKD in FLD, but medians are not abnormal, so not a disease feature as such
large LDL particles enriched in TG and UC: mentioned once, rarely measured
worsening of nephrotic syndrome after infections: a trigger, not a feature
notes: Features of FLD (complete deficiency) and FED (partial deficiency, fish-eye disease) both count. The review classifies patients by phenotype, so all renal features (proteinuria, hematuria, nephrotic syndrome, CKD and the six biopsy items) are FLD-only by construction; FED patients had none. Six of the 20 items are kidney biopsy findings because the review gives a full histology table and biopsy is the main other organ evidence it describes; the review names no other organ involvement (e.g. no spleen, liver or nerve features in its own text, only in reference titles, which were not used). 'Nephrotic syndrome' entails proteinuria; both are kept because case reports often report proteinuria or hematuria without nephrotic syndrome and the review names both. 'Low LDL cholesterol or apolipoprotein B' is a between-form difference (lower in FLD than FED) rather than a value the review calls abnormal; reviewers may prefer to swap it for glomerular C3 or IgM deposits. Two lipid-esterification markers (elevated unesterified cholesterol, reduced cholesteryl ester fraction) are kept as separate measurements; they are related but reported separately in papers.
